antiphonae_evangelicae.benedictus: Qui fácit voluntátem Patris mei, qui in cælis est, ipse meus frater, et soror, et mater est, dicit Dóminus.
antiphonae_evangelicae.magnificat: Vos qui reliquístis ómnia, et secúti estis me, céntuplum accipiétis, et vitam ætérnam possidébitis.
antiphonae_evangelicae.benedictus_es: «El que cumple la voluntad de mi Padre, ése es mi hermano y mi hermana y mi madre», dice el Señor.
antiphonae_evangelicae.magnificat_es: Vosotros, los que lo habéis dejado todo y me habéis seguido, recibiréis cien veces más, y heredaréis la vida eterna.

collecta: Deus, qui beátum Joánnem, tuo amóre succénsum, inter flammas innóxium incédere fecísti, et per eum Ecclésiam tuam nova prole fœcundásti: præsta, ipsíus suffragántibus méritis; ut igne caritátis tuæ vitia nostra curéntur, et remédia nobis ætérna provéniant.
source_note: Magnificat/Benedictus antiphons were previously the wrong shared COMMON_HOLY_MEN_WOMEN placeholder text ('pearl merchant'/'faithful servant' parables, per the shared commons.json file's own admission that this text was an uncertain reused placeholder). No individually-sourceable genuine proper antiphon could be found for this saint via live sourcing (this optional-memorial tier canonically may use the Common when no unique proper exists, confirmed by cross-check: Universalis.com itself uses this same Common-of-a-Male-Saint text for St. Louis). Replaced with a genuine, correctly-sourced Common of Holy Men and Women antiphon pair (Matt 19:29 / Matt 12:50), matching breviarium-core's own actual Common-fallback text (independently confirmed identical across Bridget, Anthony, Aloysius entries).
